composition.note: 001000 textual-history companion places formation of the Standard Babylonian recension in the late second millennium BCE and denies an exact composition date. Bounds retain the whole millennium; separate Sumerian tales in 008000 are not dated by this entry.
composition.label: Late 2nd millennium BCE · Standard Babylonian form

witness.note: 001000 identifies many surviving tablets from Ashurbanipal’s seventh-century BCE library, centuries after formation of the epic.
witness.label: 7th century BCE · Nineveh copies

setting.label: c. 2700 BCE · legendary Uruk frame
setting.note: The 001000 manuscript and its historical-setting companion explicitly place the traditional king around 2700 BCE, while denying a securely established contemporary biography. This is a legendary narrative frame, not a date for the monsters, flood, composition, or surviving tablets. Metropolitan Museum of Art: https://www.metmuseum.org/essays/gilgamesh

description: Retells Gilgamesh’s transformation from an oppressive king through his friendship with Enkidu, the Cedar Forest and Bull of Heaven exploits, and his grief-driven search for immortality. Examines Utnapishtim’s flood, the return to Uruk, and the limits of royal power; distinguishes older Sumerian and Old Babylonian material from the Standard Babylonian epic and its fragmentary surviving tablets.
